articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' in Windows Defender because apparently April showers bring vulnerability flowers. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year because Google's having a stellar security season.

articles.title: US CISA adds ‘insane’ Linux Copy Fail flaw to watch list
articles.summary: CISA adds Linux root access bug CVE-2026-31431 to their KEV catalog after discovering it's being actively exploited in the wild. Another day, another reason to question why we trusted computers with everything important.

articles.title: Silver Fox Springs Tax-Themed Attacks on Orgs in India, Russia
articles.summary: Critical cPanel authentication bypass flaw spawns a feeding frenzy of exploits after disclosure, with researchers claiming zero-day activity for at least a month prior. The internet's control panel just became everyone's control panel.

articles.title: ADT data breach exposes customer information
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix confirms unauthorized access to their source code repository because nothing says 'trust us with your security' like getting your own code stolen. The irony meter just exploded.

articles.title: Shut Down Turnkey Totalitarianism
articles.summary: Germany finally doxes 'UNKN,' the mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware groups, revealing 31-year-old Russian Daniil Maksimovich Shchukin. The mystery hacker who terrorized the internet now has a LinkedIn profile picture.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower William Binney warns about the 'turnkey totalitarian state' as EFF fights to dismantle the surveillance empire. Because apparently we built Big Brother a really nice infrastructure and now we're shocked he moved in.

articles.title: RMM Tools Fuel Stealthy Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes into effect next week, proving that lawmakers still think they can legislate away digital privacy with the technological sophistication of a potato. Expect VPN usage to surge faster than Utah legislators can spell 'encryption.'

articles.title: Week in review: High-severity LPE vulnerability in the Linux kernel, cPanel 0-day exploited for months
articles.summary: CitizenLab exposes sophisticated telecom surveillance campaigns by commercial surveillance vendors exploiting mobile operator infrastructure. Your phone calls have more surveillance than a reality TV show.

articles.title: Five Eyes spook shops warn rapid rollouts of agentic AI are too risky
articles.summary: Research shows voter data can be cross-referenced to identify military families and other sensitive targets, turning democratic participation into a privacy nightmare. Democracy dies in daylight when your vote becomes a doxxing vector.

articles.title: Trump’s Killing Spree Isn’t Stopping the Flow of Drugs Into the U.S.
articles.summary: North Korean hackers now control 76% of all stolen cryptocurrency in 2026, pulling off historic heists with AI assistance. The Hermit Kingdom has become the world's most successful crypto hedge fund through pure criminal innovation.
